title: ExplorerState
description:
The complete state of the Unified Modal - identity pillar 1. Text, Image, Video and Browse are FOUR MODES OF ONE MODAL, not four pages. There is no separate image-search page and no separate video-search page; only `mode` changes.

THE CENTRAL INVARIANT (INV-EXP-1): switching `mode` NEVER resets `intent`, `pinned_reference_ids`, `mix`, `difference` or `filters`. A mode switch changes which input surface is visible and nothing else. This is why `query` holds the payload of ALL FOUR modes simultaneously rather than one polymorphic payload: going text -> image -> text restores the typed text untouched, because it was never discarded. The modal also never closes mid-exploration: `open` is set false only by an explicit user dismissal, never by a search, an upload, an analysis or a navigation.

What a mode switch MAY reset: `results` (a new mode implies a new retrieval) and `ui.active_panel`. Nothing else.

id.description: exp_<slug>. Present when the session is persisted or shared.

mode.description: The ACTIVE input surface. text = type a description. image = drop/pick a still. video = drop/pick a clip. browse = pick visually from the taxonomy grid, the AI-free path that answers 'I don't know what Low Angle means, let me choose it visually'.

open.description: Modal visibility. Only an explicit user dismissal may set this to false.

query.description: All four mode payloads plus the shared filters, held together so a mode switch is lossless.

intent.description: The live, user-editable VisualIntent. Always the full chip form. Survives every mode switch, every search and every back/forward navigation.

selected_reference_id.description: The reference open in the detail panel. Selection is transient and MUST NOT imply membership in the mix - USE / EXTRACT are explicit actions.

pinned_reference_ids.description: The pin tray. Pinned references survive new searches, mode switches and result-set replacement. INV-EXP-4: every reference_id appearing in mix.references MUST also appear here, so a contributing reference can never vanish from the UI.

mix.description: The live ReferenceMix. Accumulates across modes; never reset by a mode switch or a new search.

prompt_mode.description: Formatter target for the live preview.

prompt_preview.description: Last rendered prompt, kept so the composer panel can show blocked slots without re-running the formatter.

query.description: Holds every mode's input at once. `mode` selects which one is active; the others are preserved verbatim.

text.description: TEXT mode input. Never cleared by switching to image/video/browse.

browse.description: BROWSE mode input: where the user is inside the taxonomy grid.

keyword.description: AI-free keyword search over taxonomy labels, aliases and related nodes and over reference titles, tags and aliases.

filters.description: SHARED across all four modes and preserved across mode switches.

expansion.description: Query expansion state. With AI off this is alias/related-hop expansion over the taxonomy only - no model involved.

expanded_ids.description: Taxonomy ids added by expansion. Any chip they produce carries source='query_expansion' and is removable in one click.

media_query.description: A still supplied as the query. Either an already-known reference or a local upload; the bytes never appear here.

upload_id.description: Handle to locally held bytes. Local-first: an upl_ handle never implies the media left the device.

thumbnail_url.description: Local object URL or remote thumbnail for display only.

analysis_status.description: 'mocked' is a first-class v0.1 state: the upload UI ships before real analysis exists.

proposals.description: The IMAGE proposal tray. Analyzer output STAGES here and nowhere else; it reaches `intent` only through ACCEPT_PROPOSAL, and REJECT_PROPOSAL removes it from this array only.

video_query.description: A clip supplied as the query. Adds the temporal window that a still cannot have.

t_start_s.description: Start of the analysed window. Lets the user say 'describe THIS camera move', not the whole clip.

proposals.description: The VIDEO proposal tray. Same staging rule as the still tray; these chips additionally carry `evidence.t_start_s`/`t_end_s`, so a camera_motion proposal points at the window it was read from.

proposal.description: One staged analyzer output. 'AI output is a proposal, never a commitment' is structural here: a proposal is a fully formed IntentChip that is NOT part of `intent` yet, held together with the category it would land in because a chip does not name its own category. A proposal's `chip.id` is mandatory - it is the `chip_id` that REJECT_PROPOSAL addresses - and `chip.alternatives` supplies the swap menu.

category.description: The VisualIntent array the chip is offered for; ACCEPT_PROPOSAL adds it there via the normal ADD_CHIP path.

chip.description: The proposed chip, already carrying source (analyzer_image / analyzer_video), confidence and evidence. Never written into `intent` by staging alone.

filters.description: Structured retrieval filters. Persist across mode switches and are recorded in every history entry so a search is exactly replayable.

license.description: Default = defaultLicenseFilter(), the allowed-by-default set of LICENSE_POLICY LP-5; user_owned is in it so the local-first path does not filter out the user's own media. cc_by_sa is opt-in; NC/ND/unknown/proprietary are excluded by default.

status.description: Default 'approved' only: an unverified reference never reaches a normal search result.

has_camera_motion.description: Video only. True restricts to references with a non-empty camera_motion attribute set.

require_categories.description: Only return references that actually carry values in these categories - e.g. require camera_motion when hunting for a camera move.

result_set.description: Retrieval output. Retrieval and analysis are separate modules: the analyzer understands, the retriever ranks; nothing here ever writes back into `intent`.

query_id.description: Correlates a result set with the request that produced it, so a slow response for an abandoned query can be discarded.

score.description: Fused score. Comparable only within one result set.

score_breakdown.description: Per-signal contributions, kept so ranking is explainable and so the 60/40 fusion default can be tuned visibly. Values are the NORMALIZED, PRE-WEIGHT ones. `null` means the signal did not exist for this item ('no embedding for this reference'), which is distinct from 0 ('it existed and scored zero') - the UI must render the two differently, and per-item weight renormalization keys off exactly that distinction.

matched_categories.description: Which categories actually matched. Drives the 'why did this come back' badges and the KEEP/CHANGE readout.

differs_categories.description: Categories deliberately different from the anchor, populated by Search by Difference.

ranking.description: The hybrid ranking configuration actually used. Recorded per result set so a replayed history entry reproduces the same ordering.

mode.description: With AI off the only reachable modes are metadata_only and keyword_only, and the product is still complete.

embedding_key.description: Which Reference.embeddings key was queried. Null with AI off.

history.description:
Navigation history of the exploration. Semantics are browser-like: pushing a new entry while cursor < entries.length-1 TRUNCATES the forward tail and then appends. back() decrements the cursor, forward() increments it; neither pushes.

INV-EXP-3 - history is NAVIGATION history, not document history. back()/forward() restore mode, query, filters and the result set. They do NOT touch pinned_reference_ids or mix, and by default they do NOT overwrite the live intent: going back to an earlier search must never delete the outfit you already collected. Restoring an entry's intent is an explicit action (restoreEntry(entry, { apply_intent: true })) or an opt-in via restore_intent_on_navigate.

cursor.description: Index of the current entry; -1 when the history is empty.

max_entries.description: FIFO eviction from the front when exceeded; cursor is decremented accordingly.

restore_intent_on_navigate.description: Opt-in: make back/forward also replace the live intent with the entry's snapshot. Off by default so exploration accumulates.

history_entry.description: A fully REPLAYABLE navigation step: replay(entry) = set mode, query and filters, then re-run retrieval with intent_snapshot and difference_snapshot. Nothing outside the entry is needed.

query.description: The full multi-mode query object as it stood, so replay is exact.

intent_snapshot.description: Deep copy of the intent used for THIS retrieval. Full chip form, so provenance is preserved in the snapshot too.

origin.description: Why this step happened. Drives the history breadcrumb text ('similar lighting to img_x') and analytics. back/forward NEVER create an entry, so they are not values here.

origin_reference_id.description: The card the step came from, for reference_* and search_by_difference origins.

origin_categories.description: Which categories the EXPLORE/EXTRACT action targeted ('same lighting', 'same pose').

result_ref_ids.description: Optional cache of the result ids so back() can render instantly before re-running retrieval.

ranking_snapshot.description: Optional copy of results.ranking so a replay reproduces the exact ordering. Open on purpose: a run using non-default fusion-ranker tuning constants records the effective {...ranking, ...tuning} pair here, and it is the one place a replay reads them back from.

difference_snapshot.description: The Search by Difference state that was in force for THIS retrieval, recorded by every step whose origin is search_by_difference, reference_explore or reference_use, because difference.keep is a hard pool filter and so is a retrieval input like intent. Read by replay() as an input only and NEVER written back into state.difference: INV-EXP-3 keeps difference a document-tier value that back/forward must not touch.

difference.description:
Search by Difference (v0.5, the key differentiator). The user marks which categories must stay the same and which must change: 'keep composition + lighting + camera, change clothing' finds the same framing/lighting/camera with a different outfit.

INV-EXP-5 (code-enforced, not expressible in JSON Schema): keep and change MUST be disjoint. A category in neither set is simply unconstrained.
Query construction: KEEP categories become hard structured filters pinned to the anchor's values; CHANGE categories become a soft overlap penalty against the anchor's values (lambda = tuning.change_lambda, default 0.7) plus a hard requirement that the category be present at all (filters.require_categories) plus a diversity boost on the CHANGE axis, and NEVER a filter on values (SEARCH_ARCHITECTURE.md 7.4 and D9; INV-SRCH-3 - a filter is never implemented as a penalty, nor a penalty as a filter); unlisted categories are free.

anchor_reference_id.description: The reference the difference is measured against. Null means the live intent is the anchor.

change_targets.description: Optional directed change: 'change clothing TO streetwear' rather than merely 'not this outfit'. category -> desired taxonomy ids.

strictness.description: How hard the KEEP constraint is applied: 1.0 = exact taxonomy match required, lower values allow sibling nodes.

ai_settings.description: AI is OPTIONAL. INV-AI-1: with enabled=false the product is still complete - browse cards, manual selection, keyword search over tags/aliases/related, metadata search and the prompt composer all work, and results.ranking.mode falls back to metadata_only/keyword_only. INV-AI-2: no model name is ever hardcoded; every capability is reached through an adapter id resolved at runtime.

enabled.description: Master switch. False is a fully supported product state, not a degraded one.

expansion_enabled.description: Alias/related-hop expansion needs no model and stays available with AI off.

adapters.description: Opaque adapter instance ids. Core code never branches on their values.

external_transmission.description: Privacy. Local-first by default; any transmission of user media to an external service must be disclosed in the UI before it happens.

ui_state.description: Purely presentational. Never affects retrieval, intent or the prompt - the brief forbids coupling the UI to the prompt engine or the search.
